claims.text: The starting alloy is near-equiatomic Nb-Ta-Mo-W-V, approximately 20 at.% of each element.
O, N, and C interstitial impurity levels can be minimized to below 100 ppm in the elemental powder blend.
SEBM or LENS can fabricate refractory high-entropy alloys from blends of elemental powders.
An AM energy density of 15–20 J/mm with preheating at 900–1000 °C will minimize thermal gradients and prevent cracking.
The AM process produces cooling rates of 10^4–10^6 K/s.
Vacuum annealing at 1250 °C for 24 hours will homogenize the alloy and dissolve segregation.
Aging at 800 °C for 4 hours can precipitate fine strengthening phases without detrimental coarsening.
The proposed route will produce a predominantly single-phase BCC microstructure with grain size below 10 µm.
The proposed processing route will suppress chemical segregation and interstitial-impurity clustering.
The aged microstructure may contain nanoscale secondary precipitates.

Alloying brittle Mo and W with subgroup IV or V transition metals can induce Jahn–Teller-related electronic-structure changes that shift elastic instability from tensile to shear failure and enhance intrinsic ductility.
Reducing grain size in polycrystalline BCC metals improves plasticity and creep resistance through a Hall–Petch-type effect.
AM rapid solidification followed by high-temperature homogenization will refine the alloy's grain size.
High-temperature annealing mitigates both segregation and porosity in comparable refractory high-entropy alloys.
The processed alloy will have room-temperature yield strength above 800 MPa.
The processed alloy will retain yield strength above 400 MPa at 1000 °C.
The processed alloy will exhibit room-temperature elongation to failure above 10%, representing a brittle-to-ductile transition.
The processed alloy will exhibit a creep rate below 10^-8 s^-1 at 1000 °C and 200 MPa.
Conventional cast or as-built refractory high-entropy alloys typically have less than 2% room-temperature elongation.
The proposed behavior may fail when interstitial impurities exceed 200 ppm.

contradictions.description: The target is described as single-phase BCC, while the aging step is intended to precipitate secondary strengthening phases and the mediator allows nanoscale precipitates. A precipitate-bearing state is not strictly single-phase, although it could still be predominantly BCC.
